n: Habakkuk takes his post like a watchman on a tower, waiting for God’s reply. After asking hard questions, he waits patiently for revelation.

f.w: I will stand upon my watch

f.g: Corrected — or answered regarding his complaint.

n: The Lord answers: write the vision clearly on tablets so a messenger can read it easily as he runs to spread it.

f.g: Tablets — clay, stone, or wood writing surfaces.

f.w: that he may run that readeth it
f.g: So that a herald can read it quickly and carry it.

n: The vision is for an appointed time. It may seem slow, but wait — it will surely come. God’s timing is certain even when it isn’t ours.

f.w: though it tarry, wait for it

n: The heart of the book: the proud are not upright, but the righteous will live by faith — or faithfulness. Paul built his teaching on this verse.

f.w: the just shall live by his faith

f.g: Hebrew emunah — steady faithfulness, trust that holds firm.

n: The arrogant conqueror, like a drunk who never stays home, is as greedy as the grave — never satisfied, gathering all nations to himself.

f.g: Sheol, the grave, which always swallows more.

n: The first of five “woes”: the conquered nations will taunt Babylon. Woe to the one who piles up stolen goods and loads himself with debts. How long can that last?

f.g: Heavy pledges or debts — piles of goods taken as collateral.

n: Suddenly the victims will rise up like creditors; they will plunder the plunderer.

f.g: There’s a pun: “biters” also means “creditors” (those who charge interest).

n: Because Babylon looted many nations, the survivors will loot it, for all its bloodshed and violence.

f.w: all the remnant of the people shall spoil thee

n: Second woe: to those who build their homes with dishonest gain, trying to set their nest high out of reach of disaster.
By destroying many peoples, they have brought shame on their own house and forfeited their own life.

f.g: Endangered or forfeited your own life.

n: The very stones and beams of their mansions will cry out as witnesses against them, since they were built with stolen wealth.

f.w: the stone shall cry out of the wall

n: Third woe: to those who build a city with blood and injustice.
The Lord has decreed that empires built this way labor only to fuel the fire, wearing themselves out for nothing.
A glorious contrast: someday the whole earth will be filled with the knowledge of the Lord’s glory, as water fills the sea. Human empires pass; God’s glory endures.

f.w: the earth shall be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD

n: Fourth woe: to one who gets a neighbor drunk to shame and exploit him. Babylon intoxicated and humiliated nations.
Babylon will be filled with shame instead of glory. It must drink the cup of the Lord’s judgment and be exposed in disgrace.

f.w: the cup of the LORD's right hand

f.g: Be exposed as uncircumcised — outside God’s covenant.

n: The violence Babylon did to Lebanon’s forests and wildlife will come back on it, along with the bloodshed against people and cities.

f.g: Babylon cut Lebanon’s cedars for its buildings and hunted its wildlife.

n: What good is an idol made by human hands? It teaches only lies. The maker trusts in a speechless object he made himself.
Fifth woe: to those who tell wood, “Wake up!” and stone, “Teach us!” It may be covered in gold, but it has no breath of life.

f.w: there is no breath at all in the midst of it

n: In contrast to silent idols, the living Lord is in His holy temple. Let the whole earth be silent before Him in reverence.

f.w: the LORD is in his holy temple
let all the earth keep silence before him
